newsitem.title: DUBAI: Chiyoda to start work on $425mln Qatar plant soon.
newsitem.headline: Chiyoda to start work on $425mln Qatar plant soon.

text.p: Japan's Chiyoda Corp will next month formalise a $425 million contract to build a petrochemical plant in Qatar and seek bidders for subcontracting work, an official said on Wednesday.

"We shall be completing a...formality in September, after which Chiyoda Corporation can go ahead with laying the foundation stone and seek bidders for various sub-contract packages," said an official at the state-run Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC).
"Chiyoda Corporation is expected to start construction next month and it will take about 32 months to be completed," the official added.
The $425 million deal covers construction of the methanol and MTBE plant for an overall project worth $600 million.

The Qatar Fuel Additives Company (Qafac), which is setting up the complex to produce an annual 850,000 tonnes of methanol and 620,000 tonnes of methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE), issued a letter of intent for the contract to Chiyoda in June.
The project is to be financed by a mix of export credits and commercial loans, arranged by foreign partners.

Foreign partners include Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp, which holds 20 percent, Canada's International Octane Ltd and the private Lee Chang Yung Chemical Industry Corp of Taiwan, which each hold 15 percent.
QGCP owns 50 percent of the project.
The project is to use 100 million cubic feet per day of North Field gas and 500,000 tonnes per year of butane, supplied by QGPC.
The Taiwanese partners have already pledged to take a third of the output besides their equity stake in the project.
The project is due to go on stream in early 1999.
